title: derive_pseudonym takes two bare &str arguments that silently swap
description:
persona-core/src/pseudonym.rs:13: `pub fn derive_pseudonym(ikm: &[u8], trust_domain: &str, consumer_app_id: &str) -> String`.

The two `&str` parameters are adjacent, interchangeable to the compiler, and semantically opposite (HKDF salt vs HKDF info). Calling `derive_pseudonym(ikm, consumer_app_id, trust_domain)` compiles, never errors, and returns a well-formed 64-char hex pseudonym that is simply wrong and stable-wrong — the failure is undetectable at every layer above, since the only property anything checks is determinism. The crate own tests (pseudonym.rs:95-99) demonstrate that swapping the arguments changes the output without any signal.

Newtypes (`TrustDomainSalt`, `ConsumerAppId`) or taking `&TrustDomain` and `&ConsumerIdentity` directly — both types already exist in this crate — makes the mistake a type error. Taking `&ConsumerIdentity` also removes the current unenforced coupling where the caller is expected, but never required, to pass `ConsumerIdentity::selector_key()` as the third argument.

Secondary: the return type is a hex `String`. A caller that needs the raw 32 bytes (to feed another KDF, or to compare in constant time) must hex-decode output the function just hex-encoded. Returning `[u8; 32]` with a separate `to_hex()` serves both without allocating.
close_reason: Both fixed together in 5205a1c, since they are two halves of one API. .52: the HKDF info input is now prefixed with the fixed label persona-pseudonym-v1:, making a future scheme change expressible (v2 derives alongside v1 during a migration) rather than silent. One label, no negotiation, no config. ConsumerIdentity::selector_key's seven format strings are the other half of that commitment and were documented as an implementation detail of a helper; the doc now states they are a wire commitment and that changing one is a scheme change. .53: derive_pseudonym now takes &TrustDomain and &ConsumerIdentity -- types the crate already had -- so the salt/info swap is a type error instead of a well-formed wrong answer, and the unenforced convention that the caller pass selector_key() is gone. It returns [u8; 32] and is crate-private; the persona_core::derive_pseudonym re-export was dropped, which no caller outside persona-core used, applying the reasoning already recorded on derive_pseudonymous_id (HKDF over public inputs is not pseudonymity). SvidSigner::pseudonymous_id is now the only entry point. Test vectors recomputed from pyca/cryptography with the oracle recorded inline, preserving what persona-5s4b.69 flags as worth keeping; one test asserts the output differs from the same inputs derived without the label. Mutations verified: dropping the label, bumping the version, and swapping salt for info each kill tests.
